lines.text: Tuner X can measure your drivetrain, test every module, and write one file for you.
Start with thirteen devices on one bus, each with its own ID, and no warnings.
Make a new swerve project, and enter four numbers: front to back, side to side, the wheel's radius, and the drive ratio. The two distance labels are easy to swap, so read them twice.
Then set up each corner. Pick its encoder and its two motors, and hold the wheel straight when it asks. That's the module's zero.
Verify each one. If the wrong corner moves, two IDs are swapped.
Generate only the constants file, and replace yours with it. Then set your team number, and deploy.
You can drive it before the robot's even finished. Run the simulator, push the stick, and watch the pose move on the field.
Three files make the drivetrain. Two come from CTRE. The third, the drive mechanism, is the one your code talks to.

Here's what's different from the arm. A drivetrain's last request is a speed, and you know a request stays on the motor. So teleop gives it a default command that reads the sticks every loop. Let go, and it sends zero.
On blocks, pushing forward lines up all four wheels. On the floor, let go of the sticks, and it stops.
Measure it, generate it, and drive it in simulation before it ever touches the floor.
